what: Claude Code hook config is read once at session start — settings.json changes mid-session don't activate new hooks in that session. Therefore `autoUpdateIfNeeded()` in the MCP server follows a "heal on first run, works on second run" pattern: the file gets rewritten correctly when the stale session launches, but the restored hooks only become active on the *next* Claude Code session in that directory. This is a Claude Code platform limitation, not an aide-memory bug. Validating auto-update (scenario H) requires two sessions: session 1 triggers the rewrite, session 2 confirms the restored hooks fire.
why: During U3/H validation I incorrectly called H "passed" after seeing the file diff, without acknowledging that the hooks weren't active in the session that triggered the update. User rightly pushed back — this is a real two-step validation that needs both sessions to prove end-to-end. Documenting so future sessions don't make the same shortcut.
